Team — taking the call notes and Elena’s reply, below are the model inputs I want to validate before we send the three scenarios to BWH. Please annotate the Drive spreadsheet if you disagree.

Key inputs (working)
- Avg tokens / feature call: 500 (prompt 80 + response 420) — add 10% overhead for headers/metadata -> 550 tokens effective
- Pilot monthly volume: 300k feature calls -> 165M tokens? (No — that math is wrong). Correct calculation: 300k calls * 550 tokens = 165M tokens -> 0.165B; but we report in 1M-token buckets -> 165 * 1M tokens
- Expansion target: 15M tokens/month (Elena said expansion to ~15M), double-check numbers; also include 50M scenario.

Cost and pricing targets
- RDW estimated inference cost (on-dedicated quantized variant): $60 per 1M tokens (includes infra, caching, routing, ops allocation). This is our internal blended cost for their workload at expected batching + KV cache hit assumptions.
- BrightWave target price: $180 per 1M tokens (customer-facing target).
- Gross margin at that price = (180 - 60) / 180 = 66.7% -> within their stated target band (~60–70%).

Per-feature math (pilot):
- Cost per feature call = 550 tokens / 1,000,000 * $60 = $0.033 (3.3 cents)
- Price per feature call (if we price at $180 / 1M) = 550 / 1,000,000 * $180 = $0.099 (9.9 cents)
- Contribution margin per call = $0.066

CAC payback sensitivity (example)
- Assume ARPA from feature = $3,600 ARR per customer that enables feature (platform/subscription uplift + seats) — adjust if finance provides different number.
- Target gross margin contribution to payback = 50% of ARPA first-year (conservative).
- If ACV = $3,600, monthly revenue = $300. At contribution margin 66.7% -> contribution margin dollars/month = $200.
- If we need CAC payback < 12 months and estimated CAC = $1,800, payback = 9 months at current ARPA/margin assumptions.

Sensitivity rows to produce
- Vary price per 1M token: $140 / $180 / $220
- Vary avg tokens per call: 450 / 550 / 900
- Vary enabled MAU %: 10% / 20% / 40%
- Output: $/feature, monthly gross contribution, unit economics per ACV bucket, CAC payback months

Questions for Karthik/Aditya
1) Can we justify $60 / 1M cost number for their workload across pilot/expansion? If not, what are the levers (quantization level, batching, cache TTL) and realistic ranges?
2) If procurement asks for a committed rate at >10M tokens/mo, how quickly can we commit to a dedicated pool and meaningful discounts?
3) Any platform constraints (rate limits, enforced batching) that would materially change tokens-per-call?

I’ve uploaded the initial model and a draft SOW. Will iterate after your notes—goal to send to procurement by EOD Friday (US).

Thanks,
Monica

Nice write-up Monica — quick notes from infra/SE lens: 

- Cost range: $50–75 per 1M tokens depending on model variant and sustained batch sizes. $60 is defensible if we run 8-bit quantized model with ~75% prefix cache hit and continuous batching. If they have many unique contexts (low cache hits) cost drifts to ~$70–75.
- Levers to present to customer: quantization (8-bit vs 4-bit), cache TTL policy (30s vs 5m), and a canary for fallback to cheaper model variant on cold starts. We should show projected costs under each lever.
- Commit timeline: we can guarantee a dedicated pool discount within 30–45 days of signature for up to 6 months. For >10M tokens/mo committed, recommend a two-tier discount: 10–30M -> 10% off list; 30M+ -> 18% off list (subject to capacity).

Action items I will take (ETA tomorrow EOD):
- Fill the infra cost tab in BWH_feature_token_model.xlsx with low/likely/high cost rows and the assumptions for cache hit, batch size, and quantization.
- Draft a short paragraph for SOW that describes pilot commitment, conversion cadence, and discovered SLAs.

If you want, I can hop on a 30-min call with Elena/procurement to walk the pilot economics.
